text.en: Thomas Helmore and John Mason Neale, signing a notice in their carol book of 1854, wrote that they gave the old music "without alteration", and that the words were "free imitations, for the most part," of ancient Christmas carols.
text.es: Thomas Helmore y John Mason Neale, en una nota que firmaron en su libro de villancicos de 1854, escribieron que daban la música antigua "sin alteración" y que la letra era, "en su mayor parte", "imitaciones libres" de antiguos villancicos de Navidad.

source.en: The Condensed Vocal Parts to the Carols for Christmas-tide (London: J. Alfred Novello, 1854), the Notice under the Index, signed "T. H." and "J. M. N." and dated "SS. Simon and Jude, 1853"; a Google scan of HathiTrust record 011630024, PDF page 10, read from the scan

text.en: Helmore's book marks each cry of "News!" in the first verse, and of "Joy!" in the second, fz, a sudden strong accent. In the last verse the two cries of "Peace" are marked p, soft, and each is held for a whole beat.
text.es: El libro de Helmore marca con fz, un acento fuerte y repentino, cada grito de "News!" en la primera estrofa y de "Joy!" en la segunda. En la última estrofa, los dos gritos de "Peace" llevan la marca p, suave, y cada uno se sostiene un tiempo entero.

source.en: The Condensed Vocal Parts to the Carols for Christmas-tide (London: J. Alfred Novello, 1854), No. VI, "Good Christian men, rejoice.", pp. 20 and 21; a Google scan of HathiTrust record 011630024, PDF pages 26 and 27, read from the scan
